title: Runtime health signals and admission protection transitions
purpose: Find reachable failures in propagation of runtime health and progress signals into the admission protections actually promised by current contracts, including recovery and combined causes. Apply the companion evidence and ownership contract. Do not invent universal write blocking, freshness deadlines or performance thresholds; exclude static configuration, lifecycle ownership and Raft quorum algorithms.
invariants: For reachable samples and validated thresholds, disk hysteresis blocks when any sampled WAL/data volume reaches its block mark, retains the previous state in the band and clears a blocked verdict only when every sampled volume is strictly below its resume mark. Test equality separately at both boundaries; establish which nodes and measurements actually participate, rather than treating every configured peer as a successful sample (health/thresholds.go NextDiskBlocked; cli.md Server Health Check Flags).

The leader HealthChecker evaluates local and successfully polled peer disk samples plus eligible clock samples and publishes disk/skew reasons as one gate snapshot. CheckWritesAllowed must not observe a transient allow caused by torn reason publication; disk has error precedence while either cause must still reject. Recovering one cause does not clear a remaining established cause (healthcheck.go gateState/check/CheckWritesAllowed; thresholds.go writeGateErrorForState).

Sampling failure must retain the established distinction between unavailable evidence and observed unhealthy state: the collector retains previous cached values on Statfs failure; failed peer disk polls are omitted; clock RPC failures and excessive RTT do not establish skew; nil initial gate and nonleader evaluation are fail-open. Trace their actual consequences before alleging a violation. These policies do not establish an age deadline or require fail-closed behavior (diskusage.go collect; healthcheck.go check/exceedsClockSkew).

Write-gate rejection must reach the routes that actually consume Admit or Barrier before their corresponding proposal. Barrier appends a WAL no-op and explicitly shares this protection. Trace forwarding to the admission-owning leader, internal callers and each exemption by its own gate; a SetClusterPolicy exemption from policy readiness is not an exemption from every earlier guard. This is an admission-time check, not a promise to revoke previously admitted or committed work (admission.go Admit/Barrier; bootstrap module; controller and gRPC call paths).

Existing progress protections must constrain the admission work they promise: Admit waits for leader readiness before state pre-reads; policy readiness waits for a committed revision except policy-only requests; query-checkpoint creation rejects unavailable audit projection; cache-horizon rejection prevents an unreachable preload proposal. Follow rejection/wait/retry and release after the actual prerequisite changes, without treating all lag metrics as write gates or assuming identical guards on Barrier (admission.go; node.WaitLeaderReady; plan.resolve; admission-cache-horizon.md).

Disk and clock conditions gate writes, not ordinary reads or readiness. Preserve distinct probe contracts: HTTP livez, readyz, health and clusterz and service gRPC health have different inputs; service gRPC includes committed policy readiness, while Raft-server gRPC health is separately registered. A discrepancy needs the specific endpoint contract, not an assumed universal healthy bit (http/server.go and handlers; health/grpc_health_updater.go; bootstrap/module.go; companion source-conflict note).

A rejected runtime protection must preserve its established externally actionable error through the actual adapter chain: disk maps to ResourceExhausted/HTTP 429, skew to Unavailable/HTTP 503, cache horizon to operational Unavailable. Prove the selected branch and absence of its proposal, not merely any error. Local health must not alter deterministic outcomes of an already committed entry (cli.md health errors; grpc/errors.go; adapter error classifiers; deterministic-fsm.md section 3.4).
adversarial_questions: For each signal, what is the measurement source, update trigger, retained state, eligibility rule, consumer and observable admission outcome? Which lag/progress values have a promised protection and which are monitoring only?

Across healthy, block equality, hysteresis band, resume equality and below-resume transitions, does WAL or data on another sampled node keep the gate blocked? Can disk recovery plus new skew or skew recovery plus remaining disk expose an unintended allow?

After a valid sample, what does a failed Statfs, absent connection, failed disk RPC, failed time RPC, zero capacity or excessive RTT actually contribute? Is a freshness guarantee documented? Is the concern a violation of the accepted policy or a question about changing that policy?

On leadership loss and reacquisition, when is the old local verdict reset and the new leader verdict evaluated? Does a reachable routed request consume the intended gate snapshot? Keep algorithmic quorum/leadership defects and worker cancellation ownership with their neighbors.

Which external and internal operations enter Admit, Barrier, a read-only path or a separate technical proposal path? Does the claimed blocked operation really reach a proposal, or fail at an earlier unrelated guard? Establish whether bypasses are promised to be gated before calling them defects.

Does changing actual applied progress or policy/projection readiness release the matching waiter/rejection on retry, and do cancellation and failed reads surface distinctly? Is apparent lag a cache-horizon condition, leader catch-up, projection readiness or merely a diagnostic metric?

Do HTTP probes and both gRPC health registrations preserve their distinct meanings through unhealthy-to-healthy transitions? Does an old deployment description conflict with current implementation and the specific health CLI contract?

Which current guards and historical regression tests disprove the hypothesis? Can a deterministic probe distinguish the claimed transition from an earlier rejection without introducing new production thresholds or treating missing coverage as a product defect?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: During a separately authorized audit, run existing focused tests using the repository-managed validation environment and pinned Nix toolchain. Record exact HEAD, command, selected tests, setup failures and assertion reachability. The checklist proposes evidence; it does not claim execution or authorize tracked test additions, live-cluster mutation, product fixes or provider orchestration.

Existing focused evidence: go test -race ./internal/infra/health -run '^Test(ThresholdsAnyAtBlock|ThresholdsAllBelowResume|NextDiskBlockedHysteresis|WriteGateErrorForState|HealthChecker_NonLeaderResetsWriteGate|CheckWritesAllowed_NoTornStateBetweenReasons|GRPCHealthUpdater_)'; inspect what each assertion actually exercises. Atomic-state stress is not a deterministic proof of a whole sampling cycle.

Existing admission probes: go test -race ./internal/application/admission -run '^Test(AdmitRejectsWhenUnhealthy|BarrierRejectsWhenWritesBlocked|CheckQueryCheckpointProjectionReady|AdmitRejectsCheckpointWhenAuditProjectionIsUnavailable)$'; existing horizon probe: go test -race ./internal/infra/plan -run '^TestBuildPreloads_RejectsCacheHorizonExceeded$'. Verify current names and package prerequisites. These isolated guards do not prove the full routing/sampling chain.

Propose deterministic multi-cycle fixtures for block/band/resume equality, multiple nodes/volumes and disk-to-skew cause replacement. Observe the gate error, actual downstream proposal count and a successful retry after recovery; use barriers, controlled samples or fake time where available, never sleep-based transition claims. Do not fill real disks or alter the host clock.

For stale/error measurements, propose a successful measurement then one controlled collection/RPC failure then recovery; record retained/omitted data and verdict on each cycle, including high-RTT clock discard and disabled clock checks. If current seams cannot control time, report that limitation rather than claiming deterministic evidence.

Trace existing leader-readiness, policy-readiness, projection-readiness and HTTP/gRPC probe tests before selecting focused runs. Propose progress-blocked then progress-released sequences with explicit synchronization, cancellation and unchanged read/probe behavior under disk/skew. An existing mocked WriteGate test proves consumption only; an error conversion test proves mapping only.
